data.name: Junessa
data.long_meaning:
In Christian tradition, Junessa is believed to be derived from the Latin name Junia, which is derived from the Roman goddess Juno. Juno was the queen of the gods in Roman mythology and the goddess of marriage and childbirth. The name Junessa can be seen as an embodiment of the essence of Juno, representing grace, beauty, and protection.
In the Bible, there is no direct mention of the name Junessa. However, there are several references to Juno in the Old Testament, particularly in the Book of Numbers, where Juno is mentioned alongside other Canaanite gods as enemies of the Israelites. In Christian interpretation, Junessa can be seen as a reminder of the power and influence of these ancient deities, and a call to reject false gods and trust only in the one true God.
Spiritually, Junessa can be seen as a symbol of devotion and dedication to God, and a reminder of the power and beauty of the divine feminine.

in_greek.name: Τζουνέσα
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Τζουνέσα σημαίνει νέα δίκαιη και αγνή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τζουνέσα είναι παράγωγο του εβραϊκού ονόματος יונה (Yonah), που σημαίνει 'περιστέρι' και συμβολίζει την ειρήνη και την καθαρότητα. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το περιστέρι είναι σύμβολο του Αγίου Πνεύματος. Έτσι, το Τζουνέσα μεταφέρει την έννοια της πνευματικής ανανέωσης και της αγνότητας.
